mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the risk-free rate, lowering equity discount rates and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines over the prior 3 months, or the Rank IC falls below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate exceeding 0.5 percentage points from the prior month indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes a decline in corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE increases by >0.5pp from the prior month, or the Rank IC is negative over a 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in residential construction (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) indicate a broad-based weakening in the demand for goods and services, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate revenue growth slows.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline from the prior month, or the interaction effect has a Rank IC below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.5% year-over-year), a rise in the federal funds rate signals a tightening monetary policy that increases equity discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 3.5% and FEDFUNDS rises > 0.1pp from prior month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances meeting the trigger condition, or the Rank IC for the regime-triggered signal is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in employment (PAYEMS) over the past 6 months signals strong labor market conditions that support corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when PAYEMS increases over the prior 6 months, or the Rank IC falls below 0.04.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in residential construction (HOUST) exceeding 5% from the prior month indicates a weakening in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when HOUST declines > 5% from prior month, or the Rank IC is negative over a 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) over the past 3 months indicates a weakening in the manufacturing sector, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate profits are pressured.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when INDPRO declines over the prior 3 months, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in employment (PAYEMS) exceeding 100,000 persons from the prior month indicates a weakening labor market, which typically precedes a decline in consumer spending and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS declines > 100,000 from prior month, or the Rank IC is negative over a 2-year window.
